Lyman-break Galaxies (LBGs) are high-z star-forming galaxies typically selected from their lack of flux at short wavelengths. I have an ad-hoc selection I developed on a pre-release version of DP2. issues.title: Preparing training resources for Meeting Contact Persons (MCPs)
issues.body:
> 🧪 Demo copy of SprintWeek2026 issue 51 for the calendar prototype. Mentions are disabled so nobody is notified.

### Short pitch

We aim to create a set of resources that prepare MCPs for their very important roles at DESC meetings.

### Contact person(s)

John Franklin Crenshaw (@jfcrenshaw), Yuanyuan Zhang

### Sprint type

Service Sprint

### Working groups

_No response_

### Goals and deliverables

MCPs are given the important role of helping DESC members with conflicts and abuse that may arise at DESC meetings. They are not, however, usually provided with detailed information about the role and duties, nor are they provided with resources or trainings that equip them to do a good job. The goal of this sprint is to start developing some resources and training materials to fill this gap. This is the first step in a larger effort to revamp how MCPs are selected and trained.

Sprint deliverables:
1. A slide deck with resources, clarifying the role of an MCP, and providing resources that help them do their job.
2. A proposal document for how DESC should select and prepare MCPs in the future

### Prerequisites

Anyone is welcome to contribute to this sprint. Those with previous MCP experience or experience with similar roles are especially welcome!

### Communication channel and links

Slack: thread in #desc-edi; you can also message the contacts on Slack.

issues.title: HACC Hydro Sim Hackathon
issues.body:
> 🧪 Demo copy of SprintWeek2026 issue 6 for the calendar prototype. Mentions are disabled so nobody is notified.

### Short pitch

Explore a new suite of hydro sims from the HACC team, with varying cosmological and hydrodynamic parameters.

### Contact person(s)

`@AstroPatty` `@patricialarsen`

### Sprint type

General Sprint

### Working groups

CL (Clusters), SCS (Survey Computing & Simulation), MCP (Modelling and Combined Probes)

### Goals and deliverables

Whatever you want! Some possibilities:

* Pretty pictures of nice clusters
* Plots of scaling relations as a function of subgrid parameters and/or cosmology
* Shape measurements of simulated halos or galaxies
* Clustering measurements
* Measurements of galaxy colors

Whatever you want to explore in hydro sims, we can help you do it.

### Prerequisites

- Access to Perlmutter
- Beginner Python knowledge

### Communication channel and links

Slack: #opencosmo

### Detailed description

The SCIDAC 400 suite is a set of 110 hydrodynamic simulations with varying cosmologies and subgrid parameters. They serve as a great laboratory for exploring the effects of hydrodynamics on structure formation, building emulators, or just getting your feet wet working with simulation data. Simulations are 400 Mpc/h boxes.

This sprint is beginner-friendly. We will provide both scientific and technical support, and extensive software tooling for working with the data. This is a great way to prepare for the upcoming release of the [Frontier-E](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.03557) simulation, the largest hydro sim ever performed.

### Options

- [X] New contributor friendly

### Wrap-up

_No response_

issues.body:
> 🧪 Demo copy of SprintWeek2026 issue 58 for the calendar prototype. Mentions are disabled so nobody is notified.

### Short pitch

DEED has a prototype implementation of its visualization aspect that we'd like to make usable for the larger community.

### Contact person(s)

Leo Sajkov

### Sprint type

General Sprint

### Working groups

MCP (Modelling and Combined Probes)

### Goals and deliverables

- A stable visualization interface that can take a variety of inputs (data vectors, MCMC chains, etc.) and produce the appropriate plots
- Overplot inputs from different data products
- Reach goal: make the plots interactive, to allow for easily comparing between different data products

### Prerequisites

Most of this project is vibe-coding, so enthusiasm and creativity with regard to visualizing data products is most useful!

### Communication channel and links

Slack: #desc-de-dashboard
Repo: https://github.com/LSSTDESC/DEED

### Detailed description

DEED's visualization aspect is built to flexibly plot different data products that are either stored in the Data Registry or passed as input by the user. This aspect becomes most powerful when it can overplot multiple data products so that they can be compared. Paired with good data provenance, this becomes a great way of understanding how choices in modeling, data, assumptions, etc., propagate into results.

- [X] New contributor friendly

_No response_
